title: Building an ACP-Compatible Agent Live — Bennet Fenner, Zed
talk_summary: Bennet Fenner from Zed live-codes a minimal ACP-compatible coding agent in TypeScript, showing the four required interface methods (initialize, authenticate, newSession, prompt), streaming session updates for text and tool calls, and proxying filesystem/terminal capabilities to the client. The talk is primarily a protocol tutorial for editor-agent interoperability, not an efficiency or orchestration talk.

takeaways.technique: Thin standardized agent-client protocol (ACP) over JSON-RPC/stdio
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents implement a small fixed interface (initialize, newSession, prompt, cancel) and stream typed session updates (message chunks, tool call start/update, diffs) so any client can drive any agent without bespoke glue.

Instead of the agent touching the local FS directly, the client advertises fs/terminal capabilities and the agent proxies reads/writes/exec over the protocol, so the client controls the environment and sees unsaved state.
takeaways.evidence_quote: ACP actually proxies the file system too. Like the client can provide a uh a file system capability

takeaways.technique: Structured tool-call lifecycle events with diffs
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent emits a tool-call session update (title, status in-progress, locations), then tool-call updates with status and content; edits are sent as old/new text and the client computes the diff.
